title: Register for Maryland paid family and medical leave (FAMLI)
summary: Every employer with at least one employee in Maryland must register with the state's paid family and medical leave program (FAMLI). There are no exceptions. Contributions start on wages paid from January 1, 2027.
action: Register at paidleave.maryland.gov. An authorized officer of the business (such as the owner, partner, or CEO) must do the first registration. Payroll companies and accountants can't register for you, but you can give them access afterwards.

deadlines.label: FAMLI contributions start on wages paid

title: Collect and pay FAMLI contributions every quarter
summary: From January 1, 2027, the FAMLI rate is 0.9% of each Maryland employee's wages (up to the Social Security wage cap). You may withhold up to half (0.45%) from employee pay. You file a Quarterly Wage and Hour Report and pay by the last day of the month after each quarter.
action: Set up payroll to withhold the employee share starting with January 2027 pay. File your first quarterly report and payment for January to March 2027 wages by April 30, 2027.

deadlines.label: First FAMLI quarterly report and payment due (Jan to Mar 2027 wages)

title: Pay the FAMLI employer share (15+ employees)
summary: Employers with 15 or more employees must pay the full 0.9% FAMLI rate: the 0.45% employee share plus a 0.45% employer share. Size counts every employee under your federal tax ID (EIN), in all states. Employers with fewer than 15 only send the employee half.
action: Budget for the employer share of 0.45% of Maryland wages. During 2027, FAMLI decides your size each quarter from your wage reports, so a quarter with fewer than 15 employees gets the lower rate.

deadlines.label: First FAMLI quarterly report and payment due (Jan to Mar 2027 wages)

title: Give employees FAMLI notices
summary: You must tell employees about paid family and medical leave starting in July 2027 (six months before benefits begin), when you hire someone, once a year, and when an employee asks for or takes leave.
action: Plan to send the first FAMLI notice to all employees in July 2027, and add it to your new-hire paperwork and yearly notices.

title: Decide whether to use a FAMLI private plan
summary: Instead of the state plan, you can offer paid leave through an approved private insurance plan. To skip state contributions during 2027, you must file a Declaration of Intent between September 1 and November 15, 2026. Most small businesses stay on the state plan.
action: Only if you want a private plan: have a licensed insurance agent sign the Proof of Private Plan Consultation form, then have an authorized officer submit the Declaration of Intent in your FAMLI account by November 15, 2026. Otherwise, do nothing and you stay on the state plan.

deadlines.label: FAMLI private plan Declaration of Intent window closes
